thought_title: Where the Bishop Is, Let the People Be

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Πάντες τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ἀκολουθεῖτε, ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρί, καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ὡς τοῖς ἀποστόλοις. τοὺς δὲ διακόνους ἐντρέπεσθε ὡς θεοῦ ἐντολήν. μηδεὶς χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου τι πρασσέτω τῶν ἀνηκόντων εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν. ἐκείνη βεβαία εὐχαριστία ἡγείσθω, ἡ ὑπὸ ἐπίσκοπον οὖσα ἢ ᾧ ἄν αὐτὸς ἐπιτρέψῃ. [2] ὅπου ἂν φανῇ ὁ ἐπίσκοπος, ἐκεῖ τὸ πλῆθος ἤτω, ὥσπερ ὅπου ἂν ᾖ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, ἐκεῖ ἡ καθολικὴ ἐκκλησία. οὐκ ἐξόν ἐστιν χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου οὔτε βαπτίζειν οὔτε ἀγάπην ποιεῖν: ἀλλ’ ὃ ἂν ἐκεῖνος δοκιμάσῃ, τοῦτο καὶ τῷ θεῷ εὐάρεστον, ἵνα ἀσφαλὲς ᾖ καὶ βέβαιον πᾶν ὃ πράσσετε.
pass_a_gloss: [1] All of you, follow the bishop as Jesus Christ follows the Father, and follow the presbytery as the apostles; and respect the deacons as the commandment of God. Let no one do anything that concerns the church apart from the bishop. Let that Eucharist be considered valid which is under the bishop or under one to whom he entrusts it. [2] Wherever the bishop appears, there let the people be, just as wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic church. It is not permitted apart from the bishop either to baptize or to hold a love feast; but whatever he approves, this is also well-pleasing to God, so that everything you do may be secure and valid.
pass_b_english: Every one of you, follow the bishop, as Jesus Christ follows the Father. Follow the presbytery as you would the apostles. Honor the deacons as you would God's own command. Let no one do anything that belongs to the church without the bishop. Let that Eucharist be held valid which is under the bishop, or under someone he has entrusted with it.

Where the bishop appears, there let the people be, just as where Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic church. Without the bishop it is not permitted either to baptize or to hold the love feast. But whatever he approves is pleasing to God as well, so that everything you do may be sure and valid.

choices.why: First surviving use of the phrase; lowercase 'catholic' keeps the sense 'whole, universal' without a later denominational label.

choices.english: Honor … as you would God's own command
rejected: as being the institution of God (ANF)

choices.english: Let that Eucharist be held valid
choices.why: βέβαιος = firm, valid; the third-person imperative ἡγείσθω is kept.
rejected: The Eucharist you can rely on (drops the imperative)

choices.why: ἀγάπη with ποιεῖν names the common meal, not the virtue.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF's 'institution of God' for ἐντολή and 'proper Eucharist' are looser.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked in full, including sections [1] and [2]. Source is Smyrnaeans 8 (catholic-church sentence; no scripture quotation, so no citation was required). Pass A keeps both the jussive and the purpose clause. Pass B does not: Greek 'ἵνα ἀσφαλὲς ᾖ καὶ βέβαιον πᾶν ὃ πράσσετε' and Pass A 'so that everything you do may be secure and valid' become 'Then everything you do will be sure and sound.' Greek 'ἐκείνη βεβαία εὐχαριστία ἡγείσθω, ἡ ὑπὸ ἐπίσκοπον οὖσα' and Pass A 'Let that Eucharist be considered valid which is under the bishop' become 'The Eucharist you can rely on is the one under the bishop'. Other clauses (follow bishop and presbytery, respect deacons, church acts, baptism and love feast, episcopal approval) match in sense. Title names the thought. ἤτω is disclosed.
reasons: Pass B turns the purpose clause into a future result: Greek 'ἵνα ἀσφαλὲς ᾖ καὶ βέβαιον πᾶν ὃ πράσσετε' and Pass A 'so that everything you do may be secure and valid' versus Pass B 'Then everything you do will be sure and sound.'

Pass B drops the imperative of regarding the Eucharist as valid: Greek 'ἐκείνη βεβαία εὐχαριστία ἡγείσθω, ἡ ὑπὸ ἐπίσκοπον οὖσα' and Pass A 'Let that Eucharist be considered valid which is under the bishop' versus Pass B 'The Eucharist you can rely on is the one under the bishop'.
